text: If two fair coins are flipped and at least one of the outcomes is known to be a head, what is the probability that both outcomes are heads?
solution: The four outcomes HH, HT, TH, TT are equally likely. The information 'at least one is a head' removes TT and leaves the three outcomes HH, HT, TH. Only HH has two heads, so the conditional probability is 1/3. The formula route gives the same number: P(both heads and at least one head)/P(at least one head) = (1/4)/(3/4) = 1/3. The distractor 1/2 is the answer to the different question in which one named coin is known to be a head.
source_label: GATE Overflow question page - GATE CSE 2011 Q.3, with the four options and several community solutions
answer_evidence: GATE Overflow's accepted answer records the answer as option A, 1/3, by both the reduced-sample-space count and the Bayes formula, and the page reproduces the four options as printed in the paper.
